deploy_bundleInstructions:
Bundle: {file}
Includes all images needed by selected services, including self-hosted middleware.
With SSH access, first edit deploy-target.json in the same delivery directory using its _comments, then run deploy.ps1 (Windows) or deploy.sh (Linux/macOS) there. Both read this JSON; the sh entry also requires local awk.
For isolated servers, copy the entire delivery directory to Linux and run sh deploy-local.sh there. It extracts the archive, applies it and preserves logs. An optional first argument overrides the server deployment directory.
If you copy only the archive to Linux, extract it and read APPLY.txt next to apply.sh.
Linux requires Docker/Podman, Compose, sh, tar, sha256sum, awk, curl, util-linux flock and filesystem/container permissions on a filesystem supporting flock.
Never delete or replace .deploy.lock; its lock releases after every holder exits or the server restarts. Inspect execution and recovery state after forced termination.
Partial updates require a successful full installation with matching ports/layout. Steps return nonzero on failure; result-DEPLOYMENT_ID.json records the outcome.
The bundle contains private runtime configuration; transfer it securely.
Included images:
{images}
deploy_bundleApplyGuide:
Run apply.sh manually on the Linux server

The default deployment root is {directory}. The bundle selects {runtime} as its container runtime. Auto prefers available local Podman. Use the same account, engine, and root for updates to an existing installation. An incremental bundle requires a successful full installation.

Use Docker Compose v2 or Podman with podman-compose 1.6.0 or newer, with support for --pull never. Linux also needs sh, tar, sha256sum, awk, curl, mktemp, util-linux flock, a filesystem that supports flock, and permission to write the deployment root and manage containers.

If you already extracted the archive, enter the directory containing apply.sh. Otherwise, run these commands from the directory containing the archive to extract it into a separate temporary directory.

  umask 077
  work=$(mktemp -d)
  tar -xf {file} -C "$work"
  cd "$work"

To use the default deployment root, run

  sh ./apply.sh

To specify the root explicitly, replace the argument below with the intended absolute path. Run one form.

  sh ./apply.sh {target}

The script verifies .hai/SHA256SUMS, imports the images from images/, starts the services in the bundle, and runs health checks. On success, current in the chosen deployment root points to {deploymentId}. On failure or interruption, retain the extracted files and output. Inspect result-{deploymentId}.json, steps-{deploymentId}.jsonl, and current. Keep .deploy.lock and all data volumes. If the deployment ID was already used, check the result before creating a new bundle.

The archive and extracted files contain private runtime configuration. After confirming success, you can remove the temporary directory you extracted manually.

deploy_bundleRuntime:
Configuration files and activation
config/.env.runtime in the unpacked bundle is this release's input. It contains application configuration and may include bundled middleware candidates. Change the project environment and rebuild the bundle. apply.sh verifies the unpacked content.
{directory}/config/.env.runtime is the active configuration. Serv and SvelteKit SSR read it from the read-only /run/hai/config mount on each start.
The active file uses literal dotenv syntax and is limited to 1 MiB. Missing, unreadable, oversized, or duplicate assignments fail before startup.
{directory}/releases/{deploymentId}/config/.env.runtime records this release. Updates that only select Web or middleware copy the configuration active at the time. Inspect the root file for the active value and the matching release for a historical value.
A full deployment uses the new bundle configuration and reuses stored managed credentials. A partial update of the primary application takes external connections and application settings from the new bundle and keeps existing managed connections. A partial update that excludes the primary application keeps the active configuration. Switching between bundled and external middleware requires a full deployment.
For a temporary Node backend fix, back up and edit the active file, run docker restart <container> or podman restart <container>, and verify health and the affected feature. Put lasting changes in the project environment so the next backend release carries them. An explicit HAI_* value in the container process takes precedence.
Redeploy changes to static Web or native middleware environments, ports, mounts, Node options, Nginx routes or limits, and HTTPS assembly. A website base path change also requires a rebuild.
Recovery restores the active application file before restarting previous services. The database maintenance procedure handles password and data changes already made inside the database.
deploy_refreshCookieSecureInvalid: HAI_SERV_REFRESH_COOKIE_SECURE must be true, false, or empty. Check the selected environment and packaging process for this variable.
deploy_postgresPasswordConflict: External PostgreSQL has different passwords in HAI_DB_URL (or HAI_DB.url) and HAI_DB_PASSWORD (or HAI_DB.password). Use a complete URL or separate connection fields.
deploy_bundleVariables:
Environment variables and troubleshooting (names only)
Target environment: {environment}. Packaging priority, highest first: packaging process, .env.{environment}.local, .env.local, .env.{environment}, .env, and application YAML defaults. --env-dir selects the source directory. A field overrides its parent JSON in the same source. Higher-priority parent JSON replaces older structured fields.
Names in this bundle's config/.env.runtime (--plan lists source input names): {keys}
HAI_SERV_REFRESH_COOKIE_SECURE is a standalone process flag. Only the same name overrides it. true enables Secure, false is for controlled intranet or VPN HTTP access, and empty or absent uses the Serv environment default (enabled in production). Set HAI_SERV_CORS_ORIGIN to the actual HTTP origin. Verify login and refresh after deployment.
Example for controlled HTTP: set HAI_SERV_REFRESH_COOKIE_SECURE=false in .env.{environment}.local and configure the actual CORS origin. With a successful full deployment and a serv image artifact, run pnpm run deploy --env {environment} --bundle-only --yes --services serv from the project. Unpack on the server and run sh ./apply.sh.
External PostgreSQL uses HAI_DB_URL (a complete connection string with required authentication) or HAI_DB_HOST, HAI_DB_PORT, HAI_DB_USER, HAI_DB_DATABASE, and HAI_DB_PASSWORD. A URL takes precedence. Update the effective form when changing credentials. After updating the database account and the source environment, deploy serv or a full bundle.
HAI_CACHE_*, HAI_STORAGE_*, HAI_VECDB_*, and HAI_IAM_LDAP_* configure application connections. S3 uses separate endpoint and access credentials. External or cloud-provisioned services normally have no native container variables in this bundle.
For bundled PostgreSQL, DB_PASSWORD in managed-secrets.env supplies HAI_DB_URL for the application and POSTGRES_PASSWORD for the image. POSTGRES_PASSWORD initializes an empty data directory. Other bundled images may use MYSQL_*, RUSTFS_*, MINIO_*, or LDAP_*. Rotate existing-volume credentials in both the actual account and managed state. A container restart or recreation alone cannot rotate a database password.
NODE_ENV selects the application environment. The delivery topology determines listen settings in HOST, PORT, and HAI_SERV_SERVER_*. NODE_OPTIONS and HAI_DEPLOY_PRIVATE_PROXY come from container assembly. HAI_DEPLOY_PROVIDER_SSH_PASSWORD is used by the uploader for SSH.
Protect the archive, runtime configuration, credentials, private keys, and failure logs. When sharing with operators or AI, use variable names, sources, redacted errors, and the deployment ID.
deploy_bundleHttpOnly: HTTPS: disabled. This bundle exposes HTTP port {port}, contains no certificate attachment and will not request a certificate on the server.
deploy_bundleHttps:
HTTPS: enabled, https://{domain}:{port}; mode {mode}.
Server certificate: {certificates}/fullchain.pem; private key: {certificates}/privkey.pem. Mounted read-only at /etc/nginx/tls/.
Edit expose.https in HAI_DEPLOY_PROVIDER in the packaging environment .env.{environment}.local, or the unshadowed hai.json.deploy.provider.expose.https. Enable/disable, mode, domain or port changes require a new full bundle; editing .env.runtime and restarting does not issue a certificate for a new domain.
deploy_bundleAcme: Persistent Certbot state: {state}; current certificate entry: {state}/live/{domain}. Packaging does not contact the CA; issuance runs during server deployment, followed by automatic renewal. Public port 80 and root /.well-known/acme-challenge/ must remain reachable independently of the business context path.
deploy_bundleAccounts:
Initial account variables (names and sources only; passwords omitted):
{sources}
Applications with matching bootstrap logic use HAI_CONFIG_ADMIN_PASSWORD to create the config_admin configuration administrator. HAI_ADMIN_DEFAULT_PASSWORD, HAI_AUDIT_ADMIN_PASSWORD and HAI_BUSINESS_OPERATOR_PASSWORD belong to the other template roles.
Fullstack creation generates independent initial passwords per environment. Packaging reads the selected environment and process overrides; server deployment does not generate new application account passwords. Startup creates missing configured accounts; changing variables does not reset existing passwords or restore old roles. Custom applications without this bootstrap follow their own implementation.
deploy_bundleDirectories:
File index (server paths use the actual deployment root, default {directory})
Delivery README.txt gives an overview. deploy.sh and deploy.ps1 upload and apply over SSH. deploy-target.json selects the target, authentication, and directory. read-target.awk reads that file for scripts. deploy-local.sh unpacks and applies on the server.
In the archive, APPLY.txt describes manual deployment and configuration. apply.sh verifies, locks, imports, and starts services. manifest.json records artifacts, mode, selected services, and non-secret metadata. images/ carries OCI archives for import into the engine.
The archive's .hai/compose.json contains selected services. The installed copy is the complete merged snapshot. .hai/SHA256SUMS checks the original unpacked files. Server copies can change during configuration finalization and merge.
Compose uses .hai/middleware-runtime.env for bundled containers. The file can be empty when no native settings are needed. Retained services may refer to an older release, so follow env_file in the effective Compose snapshot. apply.sh consumes .hai/managed-candidates.env for first-install candidates.
.hai/runtime-env.mjs loads and finalizes the Node environment. Optional files include .hai/request-access.yml, .hai/web.conf, proxy scripts, and .hai/tls/ for access policies, reverse proxying, and HTTPS.
Server incoming/ holds this upload and unpacked files. releases/ holds deployment and recovery records. Protect and back up managed-secrets.env, persistent-backends, and data volumes together. .deploy.lock coordinates deployment and credential operations.
current updates after server health checks pass. result-{deploymentId}.json records the outcome and recovery state, steps-{deploymentId}.jsonl records progress, and diagnostics-{deploymentId}.log contains private startup diagnostics on failure. Check active Compose references, mounts, and recovery needs before pruning old releases.
